title: Follow-up: a backslash-named source file is silently unindexable
description: Found while working GCLI-19 item 5 (2026-11-17). Making posix() in src/snapshot.ts win32-only stops it inventing src/back/slash.ts from a legal POSIX name containing a backslash, but the symbol still never enters the index: TypeScript normalises a backslash to a path separator on every platform, so ts.createProgram asks for the normalised path, finds no such file, and drops the root silently. Measured on a scratch repo with src/back\slash.ts exporting odd: buildIndex returns files ['src/back\\slash.ts'] and symbols []; ts.createProgram over that rootName has no source file whose name contains 'back' under either the raw or the normalised spelling. The working-tree path and the --ref path share ts.createProgram, so both are affected, and the file is skipped without an unresolvedSites entry or any other signal.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A legal POSIX source file name containing a backslash is either indexed with its real path, or the run reports it (an unresolved or unsupported-file signal) instead of silently dropping it.
The answer is the same in working-tree and --ref mode, with a test in each.
